Overview

What Is Entrants Manager & Why Use It

The Entrants Manager is where a commissioner goes to see — and control — everyone who has joined the contest. It lives in the left-hand sub-navigation of the Commissioner Console alongside Email entrants and Pick log.

Think of it as contest admin, in one place: who's in, who's paid, who's missing picks, and who needs a nudge or a removal.

Why a commissioner uses this Running a contest means more than setting rules — someone has to track payment, catch entrants who haven't made their picks before the deadline, and clean up no-shows or duplicates. The Entrants Manager is the one screen that does all three, without digging through email threads or spreadsheets.

What lives under Entrants Manager

TabWhat it's for
EntrantsThe full roster — search, filter, mark paid, add notes, export, and take bulk action (email, pause, remove)
Email entrantsSend a message to all entrants or just the ones with missing picks, from your name or your Splash handle
Pick logAn audit trail of each entrant's already-locked picks by week/slate — never live or future picks — used to settle "did they actually submit it" disputes

2
Roster

The Entrants Tab

The Entrants tab is a searchable, filterable table of every entrant in the contest. Each row shows an entrant's avatar/handle, real name, email, the date they entered, how many entries they hold, how many picks they're missing, whether they've paid, and a free-text notes field.

Entrants (1) — a single active, unpaid entrant with 0 missing picks

Entrants (2) — both entrants have missing picks (shown in red); one row is selected, opening the bulk-action bar

Filter pills

Across the top: All, Active, Missing picks, Removed, Paused, Notes, No notes, Paid, Unpaid. Each pill shows a live count and narrows the table instantly — the fastest way to jump straight to, say, everyone who still owes a pick this week.

Table columns

ColumnDetails
EntrantAvatar + Splash handle
NameReal first/last name, if provided
EmailContact email on file
EnteredDate they joined the contest
EntriesNumber of entries this person holds
Missing picksCount in red when > 0 — the quickest visual flag for follow-up
PaidCheckbox — commissioner manually marks payment received
NotesFree-text field for internal reminders (e.g. "Venmo pending")
Tip Use the Missing picks filter right before each week's lock. It's the single fastest way to see exactly who still needs a reminder — no need to scroll the full roster.

A Search entrants box (top right) filters by name, handle, or email, and a Download button exports the full roster — handy for offline record-keeping or reconciling payments outside Splash.

3
Bulk Actions

Email, Pause & Remove

Checking the box next to one or more rows opens a floating action bar at the bottom of the table with three bulk actions: Email, Pause, and Remove.

Selecting an entrant reveals the "1 selected" action bar — Email (1), Pause, Remove

ActionWhat it does
Email (N)Jumps to the Email entrants tab with the selected entrant(s) pre-filled as the recipient
PauseFreezes the selected entrant's participation without deleting their history — they stop appearing as active but aren't wiped from the roster
RemoveTakes the selected entrant out of the contest entirely
Warn Remove is the more permanent of the two options. If there's any chance an entrant is coming back (late payment, temporary no-show), Pause is the safer default — it can be reversed, while Remove takes them out of the contest.

4
Per-Entry Control

Manage Entries

Clicking into an individual entrant opens their Manage entries screen — a week-by-week view of every entry that person holds, with a Make Picks button per week per entry.

Manage entries — each entry has its own row of weekly Make Picks buttons and its own three-dot menu (Pause / Remove)

This view matters when an entrant holds more than one entry: pausing or removing happens per entry, not just per entrant. In the screenshot, Entry #1 is already marked Paused while Entry #2 remains active — the commissioner controls each independently from the three-dot menu next to that entry.

Note Pausing or removing from this screen only affects the specific entry you act on. If someone holds two entries and only one is a problem (duplicate signup, wrong team, etc.), you don't have to touch the other.

5
Commissioner Actions

How Does a Commissioner Make a Pick for a Member?

Sometimes an entrant can't get their own pick in — they're traveling, locked out of their device, or they just text/email the commissioner their pick before a deadline. Splash lets a commissioner step in and submit that pick for them directly from the Manage entries screen.

Every entry has its own Make Picks button for every week — the commissioner uses the same button an entrant would use

How to do it

  1. From the Entrants tab, click into the entrant to open their Manage entries screen.
  2. Find the entry and the week that needs a pick, and click Make Picks for that entry/week.
  3. Select the pick exactly as the entrant would, then save it — it locks in the same way as a self-submitted pick.
Note Whether a commissioner can see and pick future weeks (not just the current one) depends on the contest's "Hide future picks from commissioner" setting. When that setting is on, the commissioner is limited to the same current-week visibility as everyone else, so they can't peek at or set upcoming picks in advance.
Tip Every pick a commissioner makes on someone's behalf is tracked. The Activity tab has a Pick changes sub-tab — a filtered view showing only the picks a commissioner entered for an entrant — so there's always a record of who actually made the call.
Warn Making picks for members is meant for genuine exceptions (missed deadlines, no device access), not as a routine substitute for the entrant making their own picks. Since the action is logged, treat it as a transparent, occasional assist rather than a default habit.

6
Communication

Email Entrants

The Email entrants tab sends a message straight from the Commissioner Console — no need to leave Splash or maintain a separate email list.

Email Entrants — choose a recipient group, a sender identity, and write a custom message

To — who receives it

  • All entrants (N) — includes eliminated entrants
  • Missing picks (N) — only entrants with an outstanding pick
  • Or, select specific rows on the Entrants tab first and use the Email bulk action to pre-fill just those people

From — how you appear

Choose to send as your full name or your Splash handle, whichever the entrants will recognize.

A custom message box (1,000 character limit) lets you add context — a deadline reminder, a rule clarification, anything — before hitting Send.

Tip Combining this with the Missing picks filter is the single most useful commissioner workflow each week: filter to Missing picks → select all → Email → send a one-line reminder before the deadline hits.

7
Reference

FAQ

Do I have to manually mark entrants as paid?

Yes — the Paid checkbox on the Entrants tab is set by the commissioner. Splash doesn't process contest fees for you in an Entertainment-Only contest, so this is a manual tracking step, not an automated payment confirmation.

What's the difference between Pause and Remove?

Pause freezes an entry or entrant without deleting their history — useful for a temporary situation. Remove takes them out of the contest. If you're not sure which to use, Pause is the safer, reversible option.

Can I pause just one of an entrant's entries?

Yes. From the entrant's Manage entries screen, Pause and Remove are available per entry via the three-dot menu, so you can act on one entry without touching the others that same person holds.

How do I email only the entrants who haven't made their picks yet?

On the Entrants tab, filter to Missing picks, select the entrants you want, then choose Email from the bulk action bar — or go straight to the Email entrants tab and choose the Missing picks (N) recipient group.

Will entrants see the notes I add?

No. The Notes field on the Entrants tab is for the commissioner's own reference — a place to track things like pending payments or reminders, not something entrants can view.

What does the Pick log show that the Entrants tab doesn't?

Pick log shows each entrant's already-locked picks by week or slate, used to settle disputes about whether a pick was actually submitted. It never shows live or future/in-progress picks, so it can't be used to peek at anyone's upcoming strategy early.

Can I export my entrant roster?

Yes — the Download button on the Entrants tab exports the full list, useful for offline record-keeping or reconciling payments outside of Splash.
